message: Use 'show' or 'demonstrate' for empirical evidence; reserve 'prove' for a proof.
Name the benchmark, metric, comparison set, and verified result.
State the evidence or reasoning instead of asserting obviousness.
Quantify the amount or use a scoped term such as 'many prior methods'.
'Novel' and 'new' are redundant; usually omit both and state the contribution.
Report the measured effect and uncertainty instead of an intensifier.
Specify which methods, metric, setting, and statistical aggregation.
Use causal wording only when the design identifies causality; otherwise use 'is associated with' or 'we attribute'.
Use either 'can' or 'is able to', usually 'can'.
Use 'better' and name the comparison dimension.
Use the current venue name 'NeurIPS' except in an exact historical title.
Name the measured capability, metric, and evaluation scope.
State the concrete analysis or investigation instead of using a generic LLM-style flourish.
Describe the technical contribution and evidence without promotional language.
